title: TikTok Monetization Requirements: Every Program, View Threshold and Country Rule
summary: Exact TikTok monetization requirements for views, followers, video length and countries, plus how to check your eligibility and fix a rejected application.
body_markdown:
## The 30-Day Plan to Hit 100,000 Qualifying Views


TikTok counts eligible views within a rolling 30-day window, so older views fall out as new days enter it. Plan for steady reach and viewer retention, then check recent analytics to see whether your format brings in qualifying views.


### Week 1: Build a Repeatable 1-Minute+ Format


Creator Rewards requires eligible videos to be at least one minute long. Length is a qualification rule, not a guarantee that viewers will stay. Choose a subject you can cover with a clear opening, useful explanation, and satisfying close. Repeat the structure across several topics so you can compare audience response without changing every creative variable at once.


1. Pick a topic with enough depth for a focused explanation.
2. Open with the question or tension the video will resolve.
3. Deliver the information in a logical sequence, then close with a clear takeaway.
4. Review retention and completion patterns before deciding what to repeat.


### Weeks 2-3: Retention Tactics That Convert Views Into Watch Time


Views bring people into a video; watch time shows whether they stayed. Name the viewer’s question immediately and remove long introductions that delay the answer. Use a visual change, example, or new point when the explanation moves to its next step. These choices support clarity and pacing, but no format guarantees a particular view count or program approval.


Review each post’s retention curve alongside its topic and opening. If viewers leave before the useful part, move that information earlier. If they stay through a specific explanation, make a follow-up that answers the next natural question. Use analytics to guide the next creative decision, not to assume one post will perform the same way again.


### Week 4: Posting Cadence, Stitches and Follow-Up Videos


Keep a cadence you can sustain while maintaining useful, original content. Answer comment questions with follow-up videos, and use Stitches when another video gives relevant context. Each post should stand on its own while contributing to a recognizable subject area. This gives viewers a reason to watch more than one video and gives you clearer signals about which themes merit continued coverage.


At the end of the month, review the current 30-day period rather than lifetime totals. Identify which topics, openings, and structures earned the strongest sustained attention, then use those lessons in the next cycle. A single spike can fade from the window; a repeatable format gives you a practical way to keep publishing qualifying-length videos.


### Why Watch Time, Not View Count, Decides the Threshold


The entry threshold is 100,000 video views in the last 30 days, not lifetime views. After acceptance, Creator Rewards payouts are tied to qualified views and video performance, not a flat payment for follower count. Keep threshold tracking separate from earnings expectations: TikTok’s rules distinguish eligible views from a simple account-wide lifetime total.
